chapter: Follow-up questions, Bird and the Ellington sidemen
title: Chicago radio: Earl Hines at the Grand Terrace and his early ambitions
summary: Jones names the broadcast bands he heard growing up, and says he had no musical ambition and wanted medicine.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Uh-huh. You mentioned hearing -- becoming familiar with quite a few musicians by hearing them on the radio. Tell me about the music on the radio when you were coming up in Chicago. Who all could you hear and how often and from where and --
Well, let's see, at that point Earl Hines was getting a lot of air time on NBC, from the Grand Terrace.
And I think he stayed in that club for about 12 years.

And it was nationwide, the exposure was nationwide, you know. And there was -- oh, guys like Jimmy Mundy, Tommy Young, Bud Johnson, a fellow named Scoops Skeer (phonetic), who was a great friend of John Collins. And, oh, I can't remember all the guys. That goes back awhile. Because I was still in school at that point.
You know, these were my idols and predecessors or whatever you may want to say, you know? And I was awfully happy to eventually become to work with them. I worked up the ladder a little bit, I think.
Did you have ambitions of -- at that time? Did you think that that was what you wanted to do, was --

No, I had no -- I didn't have any particular ambitions about music. I liked it. I loved it and still do, but when I went to school, gee whiz, I was studying science. I wanted to go into medicine, you know.
And they always said that musicians and doctors seemed to hang out together. We don't know. Especially jazz musicians.
You know, there seems to be a pattern. We don't know why.
